characterization_methods.key_findings: Equiaxed polygonal grain structure; preferential grain-boundary etching from κ-carbide precipitation; banding from alloy segregation.
characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal the peak-aged microstructure of the hot-rolled Fe-30Mn-9Al-1.01Si-0.9C-0.5Mo sample.

characterization_methods.key_findings: Grain refinement from hot rolling improved ductility at equivalent ultimate strengths; tensile strength increased by 200 MPa with aging; elongation fell from 54% to 14% at peak aging.
characterization_methods.purpose: Compare cast and wrought tensile strength as a function of aging time and elongation.

interfaces.interface_notes: Peak aging produced κ-carbide precipitation on austenite grain boundaries in the wrought sample.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: At equivalent ultimate tensile strengths, grain refinement from hot rolling produced better ductility than the cast material

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cast plates of a calcium-treated, low-phosphorus (0.006% P) Fe-30Mn-9Al-1.01Si-0.9C-0.5Mo steel.
Cast plates were hot rolled at 900°C to an 84% reduction in thickness.
Solution treated for 10 min at 900°C and water quenched to produce an equiaxed grain structure 10–20 µm in average diameter.
Peak aging (60 h at 530°C) produced κ-carbide precipitation on grain boundaries and lowered elongation from 54% to 14%.

unmapped_findings: The wrought (hot-rolled) sample is a calcium-treated, low-phosphorus (0.006% P) Fe-30Mn-9Al-1.01Si-0.9C-0.5Mo steel; Table I row 1 (Si 1.01, C 0.89, Mn 30.20, P 0.006, S 0.001, Mo 0.31, Al 8.85 wt.%) is the closest listed chemistry, although the text cites the alloy nominally as 0.5Mo.
Tensile strength in the wrought alloy increased by 200 MPa with aging (b0040).

Fig. 7(b) indicates the wrought sample spans roughly 16–55% elongation with UTS from just below 1200 MPa down to between 900 and 1000 MPa as elongation increases (approximate values read from gridlines).

The fully austenitic microstructure and annealing-twin/equiaxed-grain refinement behavior of hot rolling are discussed generally in the introduction (b0007, figure_001), but the explicit 50 µm average grain size in figure_001 belongs to a different hot-rolled alloy (Fe-29Mn-6Al-0.9C-0.29Si-0.44Nb-0.44Mo), not this sample.
